The Fed also adjusted its balance sheet policy, slowing the runoff of Treasury holdings to $5 billion monthly to prevent long-term yields from rising too sharply. Despite elevated uncertainty, Powell emphasized the economy remains healthy with low unemployment, though sentiment has weakened. Investors responded positively to the measured tone, with the S&P 500 rising 1% following the announcement. The central bank remains committed to patience, prioritizing clarity on economic data before making further adjustments.

The fires have caused extensive destruction, with official figures reporting at least 21 deaths and 305 injuries. Over 45,000 hectares have been burned, surpassing the area affected by the 2024 Valparaiso fires. Approximately 2,300 homes have been destroyed, leaving nearly 700 people in shelters. The tragedy has primarily impacted the Bio Bio region, including Penco and Lirquen, marking one of the worst emergencies in Chile's recent history. Authorities continue to monitor active megafires in neighboring regions of Ñuble and La Araucania.
